baseline_and_control.naive_control_match.reason: The raw-input control appends sampled IC values and a BC one-hot to the coefficient input. Its 58,700 encoder parameters closely match the structured encoder's 58,550, within the declared 1% matching rule, and both have completed own runs.

baseline_and_control.held_fixed_respecte.reason: The architectural interfaces are retained, but headline collocation counts are not fixed across the original baseline and conditioned arms. For RD, the baseline trains on 13 specifications with 1,000 collocation points each, versus 156 specifications with 1,000 each for the conditioned models: 13,000 versus 156,000 points per epoch. Equal per-specification counts do not satisfy the task's across-arm count requirement.

core_result.joint_coeff_ic_generalizatio.reason: Positive but sub-delta gains occur on both required axes in RD: 0.1800 versus 0.1857 for unseen IC parameters and 0.2039 versus 0.2058 for unseen combinations. These gains are below delta and do not beat the baseline at its trained IC. Other families include reversals or noise-dominated gains, so a clear joint result is not established.

core_result.unseen_ic_family_generalizat.reason: Gaussian and three-mode families are genuinely excluded from training. On convection–reaction, Gaussian error improves from 0.3257 to 0.3055, a 0.0202 gain below delta=0.0326; the three-mode gain is also sub-delta. The trained-IC baseline is substantially more accurate, and larger reaction-family gains are not separated from seed noise.

core_result.seen_spec_preserved.reason: Only 18 of 46 coefficient settings satisfy the prescribed per-coefficient tolerance. On convection–reaction, none of 13 passes, and mean original-IC error rises from 0.0699 to 0.1726, approximately 2.47-fold. This is a substantial regression.

conditioning_attribution.beats_naive_con.reason: The head-to-head comparisons do not establish a noise-separated structured advantage under the preregistered rule. Even the reaction Gaussian gain of 0.1674 is below pooled seed SD≈0.2143, and the denser-sensor matched control removes the apparent reaction-family advantage.

conditioning_attribution.removed_conditi.reason: Removing the correct IC while retaining coefficients causes substantial, noise-separated degradation. For convection–reaction Gaussians, shuffling increases error from 0.3063 to 0.4224; the 0.1160 increase exceeds pooled SD≈0.0217. Constant and original-training-IC replacements degrade further toward coefficient-only behavior.

conditioning_attribution.non_degenerate.reason: Direct latent diagnostics distinguish ICs, and conditioning removal changes predictions materially. In convection–reaction, between-IC variation accounts for 69.2% of structured latent variance, accompanied by positive held-out descriptor-probe performance.

boundary_conditions.multi_bc_generalizat.reason: A single model trained on periodic and Dirichlet specifications improves on the control at held-out Neumann configurations. For unseen IC parameters under Neumann BCs, errors are 0.1978 versus 0.2764: gain 0.0786 exceeds delta=0.0276 and pooled SD=0.0254. This satisfies the stated configuration-level criterion, although Gaussian/composition gains are weaker and Neumann solutions coincide with periodic solutions for the selected profiles.

boundary_conditions.reference_validated.reason: The authored solver has both required validation components: refinement convergence and periodic-overlap agreement.
